newsitem.title: BELGIUM: BELGACOM TO OPPOSE DISCOUNT FOR THIRD GSM LICENCE.
newsitem.headline: BELGACOM TO OPPOSE DISCOUNT FOR THIRD GSM LICENCE.

text.p: Belgian state telephone operator Belgacom said on Friday it would oppose any discount that might be given to the future operator of a third GSM mobile phone network in Belgium.
"If it has always been said "nine billion francs for everyone", then a discount is indeed not obvious," Belgacom spokesman Jan Margot told Reuters.

Telecommunications Minister Elio Di Rupo said earlier on Friday a third operator would have to pay about nine billion francs for the licence to the Belgian state, the same amount paid by the two existing operators.

But since the third network would use the DCS 1800 technology, which requires more investment in the antenna network than is the case for other, existing technology, the amount might be revised down, he added.
"I don't see why (the third operator) would have more investment costs. In a way they should have less costs since equipment becomes cheaper all the time," Margot said.

"The first two operators have also invested heavily to prepare the market, they have been about the biggest investors in advertising to make the GSM phenomenon known, the third operator benefits without having to invest or at least not that much," he said.
Mobistar NV, the operator of Belgium's second GSM network, declined to comment.

Eric Van Heesvelde, managing director of the Belgian Institute for Postal and Telecommunications Services (BIPT) which assesses the bids, said the ultimate goal was to ensure that none of the three operators would be discriminated.

"The final amount depends on a number of factors -- new licence conditions, investment costs, amount paid by others -- and all elements combined should lead to an honest decision, also depending of what the third candidate is prepared to pay," he said.
The government on Friday invited operators to enter bids for a third GSM network. The winner is to be selected within a year and the network is to be operational within two years.

Mobistar NV launched the second GSM network last August. Mobistar is 57 percent owned by France Telecom. Belgian data communications company Telinfo holds 10 percent and nine other Belgian companies the balance.
Belgium's first mobile service Proximus is run by Belgacom Mobile, 75-percent owned by Belgian state telephone operator Belgacom and 25-percent by AirTouch Communications Inc.
Belgium has more than half a million GSM users, with Mobistar accounting for about a fifth.
